newsitem.title: USA: Snow sweeping into southern US Plains - forecasters.
newsitem.headline: Snow sweeping into southern US Plains - forecasters.

text.p: Snow was moving into the southwest U.S. Plains Thursday morning, improving prospects for dormant hard red winter wheat crops, meteorologists said.
"We've got snow and some rains in the southern Plains," said Joel Burgio, meteorologist with Weather Services Corp. "Coverage will be good."
Burgio said three to five inches of snow could fall across the Texas and Oklahoma panhandles and western Kansas, providing cover for vulnerable wheat crops.
Farmers in those areas had been concerned about dry, blowing soil and about cold weather killing bare crops.
Snow was expected to push northeast into the southern Midwest on Friday and Saturday, bringing a chance for two to four inches of snow, Gesser said.

"This system is going to be pushing far enough east that the cloud shield is going to be covering portions of the Midwest," Gesser said. "We're going to get snow over southern Illinois, Indiana and Ohio."
Long-range forecasts suggested a cool-down for the northern Plains and Midwest toward the middle of next week but forecasters disagreed on how cold it would get.
Burgio said computer models suggested the coldest air would remain in Canada, sparing the northern United States.
But Gesser forecast three days of cold air for the Midwest with a chance for snow Tuesday through Thursday.
"The Midwest is going to get whacked again with another snow storm," he said. "There will be a three day cold outbreak and then we start getting warmer."
